title: Fill (ver 6.2)
content: **List of Contents** Duplicate Property ### **Objective** Create a realistic puffy garment by setting the fill type and weight. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Fill** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4409935066265/mceclip0.png) **Fill** **Operation** **Duplicate** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated.** ** 2. Click the piece to be applied or, Click anywhere in the 2D window ▶ Drag your cursor to select the pieces within the marquee. ** **→ The duplicated pieces appear on the mouse cursor. 3. Click the position where you place the duplicated piece. → The outlines of both pieces are sewn, and the internal lines crossed with them are sewn as well. → Display in purple. 4. Select any grey quilt lines to turn on the quilting effect. **Property** 1. Click the puffy pattern piece. **→** Filer Property appears in the Property Editor. 2. Once the puffy properties are set, simulate the garment.** ** **Property**** ** | **Description** ---|--- **Filer** | Type | Choose the type of filler. Weight | Enter the weight of the filler. **※Note:** Select multiple pattern pieces to set the total weight. The weight of each piece is calculated and distributed proportionally. Quilting Distance | Enter the quilting distance. ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4409111186457/mceclip2.png) **※Note:** Fill Volume is calculated based on the Quilting Distance and the Weight. Quilting Distance indicates the distance between the internal lines used as quilting lines, and you must input the distance value. If the internal lines are neither parallel nor their distance is constant, please enter the widest value. → You can have a reasonably realistic puffiness based on the pressure set by the weight and the quilting volume. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to duplicating and customizing puffy garment patterns in CLO 3D, focusing on fill properties and quilting effects for realistic simulation.

title: Hide Avatar
content: **Hide Avatar** \- Hide Avatars from the 3D window at your convenience. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022395347/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar. Right-click on the Avatar in the 3D window and select **Hide Avatar** from the pop-up menu. The selected Avatar will be hidden from the 3D window.
content_description: Easily hide avatars from the 3D window for a clearer view by using the Select/Move tool and choosing the Hide Avatar option from the pop-up menu.

title: Transform Graphic (2D)
content: **Transform Graphic(2D)** \- Scale, rotate or move Graphics in the 2D window. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746987/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic(2D)** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ **Transform Graphic(2D)** * **Scale Graphics **\- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746987/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic(2D)** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the Graphic to be edited in the 2D window. The **Graphic Gizmo** will appear. \- Click and drag the arrow of the Graphic Gizmo to scale the selected Graphic, maintaining the height and width ratio. \- When the desired size is achieved, release the mouse. 。 \- Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Graphic Transformation ▶ **Width** or **Height** to adjust the graphic's dimension (For detailed information, please refer to [Edit Texture](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012380188-Edit-Texture-3D-#Click4).) * **Rotate Graphics ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746987/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic(2D)** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the Graphic to be edited in the 2D window. The **Graphic Gizmo** will appear. \- Click and drag the dotted circle of the Graphic Gizmo to rotate the selected Graphic. \- When the Graphic is rotated as desired, release the mouse. * **Move Graphics ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746987/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic(2D)** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Click and drag the Graphic to move. \- When the Graphic is moved as desired, release the mouse.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide to using the Transform Graphic(2D) tool for scaling, rotating, and moving graphics in the 2D window.

title: Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)
content: **List of Contents** Select/Move Delete **Objective** Edit lines created on an Avatar. ** Location ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015215487/Edit_Line.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)** ** Operation ** **Select/Move** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015215487/Edit_Line.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)** → If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. 2. Click on the line or the shape to be selected. → The line or the shape is selected and highlighted in yellow. 3. While the line of the shape is selected, click and drag to move the selected item to the desired position. **Delete** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015215487/Edit_Line.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)** → If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. 2. Select the line or the shape to be deleted. 3. Right click on the selected item and select **Delete** or hit the Delete key on the keyboard. → The selected line or shape is deleted. **※ Note: ** * To select multiple lines or shapes, hold down the Shift-key on the keyboard, then click on additional lines or shapes. * To select all lines and shapes on the Avatar, hit the Ctrl+A on the keyboard. * After the lines and shapes are drawn on the Avatar, if you delete the Avatar, all previously created lines and shapes are also deleted. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for selecting, moving, and deleting lines created on a 3D Avatar using the Edit 3D Pen tool in the CLO 3D software.

title: Create .HW File and Register .LCN File
content: **Operation** 1. Click on the circled area to fully display the Login window. ![lcnfile0-1.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015151428) 2. Check or uncheck the circled areas according to the image below, then click on **Create HW File**. **※ Note:** When creating file, save the file name as your user ID. ![lcnfile1-1.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015151448) 3. Send the newly created .HW file to [support@clo3d.com](mailto:support@clo3d.com%C2%A0and), for a .LCN file request. 4. Download the .LCN file received from the CLO Support Team. 5. Check or uncheck the circled areas according to the image below, then click on **Register LCN File**. ![lcnfile3.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015151488) 6. title: [Property] Set Sublayer
content: ### **Objective** Assign orders to the Sewing Lines on a Pattern which folds on itself such as seam allowances and pleats in order to increase simulation stability. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001218987/________.png) **Edit Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Edit Sewing** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001218987/________.png) **Edit Sewing** → All established Sewing Lines appear in the 2D window. 2. Select the Sewing Lines to set Sublayer. → Sewing Line properties appear in the property editor. 3. Toggle on the **Set Sublayer** option. → A red arrow which indicates the order of the selected pair of Sewing Lines appear. **※ Note:** The half of the seam next to the arrow head is fixed and the other half next to the arrow tail moves according to the setting. 4. Change the Sublayer setting as needed. **Reverse Direction** | Swap the fixed Sewing Line and the moving Sewing Line. ---|--- **Front** | **Back** | Decide which side of the fabric is attached to the fixed Sewing Line. 5. Activate **Simulation**. → Changes are applied respective to the setting.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for assigning and editing sewing line orders on patterns with complex folds to enhance simulation stability in garment design.

title: [Popup] Activate/Deactivate Sewing Lines
content: ### **Objective** Activate or deactivate Sewing Lines as needed. Use this function when Sewing Lines should be applied after garment is draped such as the back slits for a men's jacket. ** Location ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001223227/________.png) Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ **Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected)** Object Browser ▶ Scene Tab ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) ▶ **Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected)** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001223227/________.png) Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ **Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected)** Object Browser ▶ Scene Tab ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) ▶ **Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected)** → Deactivated Sewing Lines appear in white in the 2D and the 3D window and their names appear in dark grey in the Scene Tab.

title: Windows - CLO Network Version Installation
content: **Objective** Install Windows - CLO Network Version. Any Asset downloaded in the previous version is maintained when a new version is installed (ver5.0.0.) ** Operation** 1. Run the DVD received upon purchase or the install file received via email. 2. After running the install file, press "Next" on the setup window to continue installation. ![1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338848/1.png) 3. Review the License Agreement and click "I Agree" to accept the terms of the agreement. ![2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338868/2.png) 4. Choose a location to install the program. ![3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338908/3.png) 5. Select a Start Menu folder. ![4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026298687/4.png) 6. The product begins installing. It takes less than a minute. ![5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026338888/5.png) 7. After the installation is completed, click "Finish" to close the window. ![6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026298667/6.png) 8. Once the program has finished installation, a Server must be set up. 9. Click the link below and check to see if the Sentinel Admin Control Center screen shows up, as it does on the picture below: [ ACC Page ](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html)[![accpage.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001356347/accpage.png) ](http://localhost:1947/)If the following screen does not appear, the HASP Driver must be reinstalled: [Manual Sentinel HASP Driver Installation ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000558507-%EC%84%A4%EC%B9%98-%ED%9B%84-%EB%B0%9C%EC%83%9D%ED%95%A0-%EC%88%98-%EC%9E%88%EB%8A%94-%EB%AC%B8%EC%A0%9C-%ED%95%B4%EA%B2%B0-%EB%B0%8F-%EB%B0%A9%EB%B2%95)As shown below, click on the "Configuration" menu on left of the ACC Page. ![configuration.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001336948/configuration.png) 10. Select "Access to Remote License Managers" as below image. ![accesstoremote.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001336928/accesstoremote.png) 11. Check the "Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses" item as shown below. Enter the IP address of the Server PC in the "Specify Search Parameters" item. Click the "Submit" button. 12. If the HASP Key can be seen as shown below after approximately 10 seconds, then the configuration is successful. ![sentinelkey.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001337068/sentinelkey.png) **※ Note:** ** Identifying Server PC's IP Address ** Start (Windows) Button ▶ All Programs ▶ Accessories ▶ Command Prompt ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' or enter 'cmd' in the 'Run' menu ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' Reference site: <http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/>
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for installing the CLO Network Version of Windows, ensuring that all previously downloaded assets are preserved during the upgrade process.

title: Slider/Puller/Stopper OBJ Registration
content: Create OBJ Register OBJ ### **Objective** Register your own OBJ file as a Slider/Puller/Stopper. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ Register OBJ** ** Property Editor ▶ Shape ▶ ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25189692962201) ** ****Operation** **Create OBJ** Check the requirements below when making OBJs in other 3D programs. **※ Essential** * Set the name of the MESH to **Slider and Puller** when creating an OBJ with a slider and a puller. ![Slider_Puller_name.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815406) * For each type, adjust the position to suit the meaning of the axis. (If the position of the axis is not correct, the OBJ may not be loaded in the correct position) Slider | X-Axis | Position the shoulder of the slider where zipper teeth insert on the X-axis 0. ---|---|--- Y-Axis | The direction the slider moves is the Y-axis, Position center of the slider where the center of the zipper teeth aligned at 0 of the Y-axis. Z-Axis | Position the Z-axis 0 where the side of the zipper teeth is located. ![Slider.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815306) Stopper | The stopper configured on both sides must be made to be the same scale as the two OBJ axes. X-Axis | Position the shoulder of the slider where zipper teeth insert on the X-axis 0. Y-Axis | **Top Stopper** Position the point where the most end (top) of the zipper blade is in contact with the Y-axis 0. **Bottom Stopper** When the slider is lowered all the way, the point where it touches the bottom of the slider is positioned on the Y-axis at 0. Z-Axis | Position the Z-axis 0 where the side of the zipper teeth is located. ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007735143) ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007735083) ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815506) Puller | Place the position where the slider is attached at the origin (0,0,0). **※Note:** The puller position is adjustable within the CLO. ![Puller.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815366) Slider & Puller | Create sliders & pullers are created based on the slider axis. ![Slider_Puller.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007734823) **Register OBJ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → The OBJ registration window appears. 2. After setting the following options, click the OK button. Basic | Type | Select the type (Slider, Puller, Stopper, Slider & Puller) to register the OBJ. ---|---|--- Name | Enter a file name. Scale | Adjust the size of the OBJ. Axis Conversion | Change each axis of the OBJ. File | OBJ | Slider / Puller | Load the OBJ file you want to register. Stopper (Top, Bottom-Open) | Load each Top and Botton-Open OBJ file. The first OBJ loaded is placed in the direction of the zipper created first. Slider & Puller (ver 6.2) | Load a combined zipper OBJ file. Select and assign the mesh item of Slider and Puller in the Select Mesh menu. Preview | Check the imported OBJ file in advance. Puller Position | Adjust the sliders on the X, Y, and Z axes to set where the puller is attached. **※Note:** This setting is for Slider and Slider & Puller types only. → The object is saved in the path below: Assets ▶ Materials ▶ Hardware_and_Trims ▶ Zipper ▶ Each object's folder
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users through the process of registering their own OBJ files as sliders, pullers, or stoppers within the CLO 3D software, ensuring proper configuration and positioning for seamless integration.

title: Avatar Measure (ver 6.0)
content: **List of Contents** Basic/Surface Circumference Measure Basic/Surface/Linear Measure Height Measure ### **Objective** Measure the circumference, length and height of the Avatar. Two methods are provided. Either based on the protruding part of the avatar or based on the surface of the curvature. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement 3D Toolbar ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360091740393/mceclip0.png) Click and hold down the Basic Circumference Measure ** Operation** **Basic/Surface Circumference Measure.** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the starting point to be measured and click the second point in the desired direction. → A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is displayed. 3. Click once more when it is in the target shape. → A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is created and the length is displayed. **Basic/Surface/Linear Measure** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the start point to be measured and double-click the end point. → A Basic/Surface/Linear Tape Measure is created and its length is displayed. → A Linear Measure runs through the Avatar by connecting the start and end points in a straight line. (ver 6.0) **Height Measure** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the point to be measured. → A Height Measure that runs vertically from the clicked point to the ground is created and the length is displayed. **※ Note:** * Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create vertical/horizontal/45˚ tilt. * Use [Attach to Measure](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000426228-Attach-to-Avatar-Tape) tool to attach the pattern outline or Internal Line to the Avatar Measure. **Go back to the List of Contents**
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for measuring the circumference, length, and height of an Avatar using two methods, ensuring precision in 3D modeling.

title: Shirring (ver5.1.0)
content: ### **Objective** Express shirring realistically by reducing mesh size of the particular area of the Pattern. **Location** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005494467/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern ▶** Select a Line**▶** Property Editor**▶** Selected Line**▶ Shirring**** ** **Operation** 1. Click on a Pattern Outline using the ![____3.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039919454/____3.jpg)**Transform Pattern** tool or ![____2.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360040742833/____2.jpg)**Edit Pattern** tool. 2. Follow the indicated path below: ** **Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶**Shirring **** ** 3. Click to toggle on the check box. → Shirring is applied to the selected line and the shirring symbol appears on the 2D Pattern. The result can be checked on the 3D Garment or on the 2D Pattern after switching the [2D Pattern Rendering Style](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360011148874-2D-Window-Display-Icons-ver5-0-0-and-Above-) to Mesh. 4. Adjust the **Interval** and **Height** of the Shirring. **Interval** | Adjust the distance between each mesh. ---|--- **Height** | Adjust the Height of the Shirring. ** ※Note:** Shirring is applied symmetrically when it is applied to Symmetric Patterns.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to realistically applying shirring to patterns in CLO 3D by adjusting mesh size and settings.

title: Sewing Tension
content: **Sewing Tension** \- Adjust sewing Tension to improve 3D Garments’ fit. \- Select the ![Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003396367/Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png)**Edit Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the Sewing Line which the sewing Tension needs to be adjusted. \- Selected Sewing Line’s properties appear in the Property Editor. * Strength : Type in a value to adjust selected Sewing Line’s Tension Strength. * Ratio : Adjust the Tension Ratio to express how various types of Sewing method influence garment drapes. **※****Note: ** The maximum Tension Ratio is 200%.
content_description: Learn how to adjust sewing tension to enhance the fit of your 3D garments by utilizing the Edit Sewing tool and modifying the properties of the selected sewing line.

title: Slider Gizmo
content: **List of Contents** Move Rotate **Objective** Move or rotate slider to adjust its distance from zipper tape. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move **** ** Operation** **Move** 1. [Create a zipper.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115004529388-%EC%A7%80%ED%8D%BC-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) 2. While the Simulation is turned off, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move** 3. Click the slider. → The slider is selected and its **Gizmo** appears. 4. Click and drag the blue segment of the **Gizmo** to move the slider back and forth. Sliders cannot be moved along with Y and Z axes. **Rotate** 1. With the**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000819148/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move** tool, click on the slider to access the Slider Gizmo. 2. Click and drag the blue circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on Y axis. Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on X axis. Click and drag the red circle of the **Gizmo** to rotate on Z axis. → The selected zipper slider rotates based on the selected circle. 3. To rotate the puller only, click on the puller while the slider is selected. → The selected puller is highlighted in yellow and the **Gizmo** changes accordingly. 4. Rotate the puller referencing #2. **※ Note:** To reset slider's position and angle, right click on the slider and select [**Reset Slider Arrangement**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-ua/articles/115004681608) option. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for moving and rotating sliders in a 3D garment design tool, enabling precise adjustments to zipper placement.

content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for editing and deleting lines on 3D garments using the 3D Toolbar.

title: Register Custom OBJ as Button
content: Create Button OBJ Register Button OBJ Create Button OBJ by Thread Type ### **Objective** Register a custom OBJ file as Button. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Register Button ** Property Editor ▶ Shape ▶ ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024299748) ** Operation** **Create Button OBJ** Please check below requirements before registering an OBJ as a button. ** ※Required: ** ** ℹ️ From CLO 7.3, no 1, 2 requirements are not necessary and can be set at registration. ** * Position the face of an OBJ towards Y-axis. * Position the contact point of an OBJ where it should be attached to 3D garments at 0,0,0 (x,y,z) coordinates. * The unit of OBJs must be in mm. e.g.) ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360033429954) ![Button_OBJ.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360033430114) Please check the attached OBJ file in your 3D modeling program for better understanding. ** ※Recommended: ** * Please maintain the number of vertices of an OBJ below 1000 to avoid speed issues. * The distance between an OBJ and the ground should be 0. (You can adjust the distance in CLO. [ Button Property Setting ▶ Thread Length (cm)](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115005617768-%EB%8B%A8%EC%B6%94-%EC%86%8D%EC%84%B1-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95)) **Register Button OBJ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → Register Button window appears. 2. After setting the following options, Click OK. **Property** | **Description****** ---|--- **Basic** | Set the name of the button file. **File** | **Size** | If the OBJ shape is different for each button size, click the + button on the top right to register as buttons of various sizes. **Size Name** | Set the size name. ** OBJ ** ** ** | Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. **Select Mesh (ver 7.3) ** | Set the mesh for the buttons and thread. ** OBJ ** | Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. **Width/Thickness** **/Weight** | Set the width/thickness/weight of the button. **Set as Default** | Set the size to be applied by default when changing with the button. **Axis Conversion (ver 7.3) ** | Switch axis of OBJ files in real time. **Preview (ver 7.3) ** | The imported OBJ file will be previewed. → The registered button is saved in the path below. CLO ▶ Assets ▶ Materials ▶ Hardware_and_Trims ▶ Button & Buttonhole ▶ Button **Create Button OBJ by Thread Type** 1. Set the name of the OBJ file for each thread type to ***_Cross.obj, *_Parallel.obj , *_Square.obj.** 2. Register the created OBJ file as a button. 3. Save the created *_Cross.btn, *_Parallel.btn , *_Square.btn files in the path below. **C:\Users\Public\Documents\CLO\Assets\Materials\Hardware_and_Trims\Button & Buttonhole\Button** 4. Run CLO and change the type of the thread in the button property window > Type > Thread Type.
content_description: This page provides a step-by-step guide for registering custom OBJ files as buttons in CLO, ensuring proper configuration and compatibility for optimal performance.

title: Transform Graphic (3D)
content: **Transform Graphic (3D)** \- Scale, rotate or move Graphics in the 3D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747647/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Material ▶ Graphics ▶ **Transform Graphic (3D)** * **Scale Graphics ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747647/mceclip0.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Select the Graphic to be edited in the 3D window. The **Graphic Gizmo** will appear. \- Click and drag the arrow of the **Graphic Gizmo** to scale the selected Graphic. \- When the desired size is achieved, release the mouse. - Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Graphic Transformation ▶ **Width** or **Height** to adjust the graphic's dimension (For detailed information, please refer to [Edit Texture](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012380188-Edit-Texture-3D-#Click4).) * **Rotate Graphics ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747667/mceclip2.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Select the Graphic to be edited in the 3D window. The Graphic Gizmo will appear. \- Click and drag the dotted circle of the Graphic Gizmo to rotate the selected Graphic. \- When the Graphic is rotated as desired, release the mouse. * **Move Graphics** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022747667/mceclip2.png) **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click and drag the Graphic to move. \- When the Graphic is moved as desired, release the mouse.
content_description: Explore the **Transform Graphic (3D)** tool to effortlessly scale, rotate, and move graphics in the 3D window for enhanced design flexibility.

title: Select
content: **List of Contents** Select Transform Pattern Tool Edit Pattern Tool Pattern Properties Deselect Select Multiple Patterns Select/Move Tool Select All **Select** \- Select patterns in the 2D and 3D windows. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022661887/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723988/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar. ** Transform Pattern Tool** * **Select with Clicks** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Hover over the pattern to be selected as its outline will be highlighted in light-blue. \- Click on the pattern. The Selected pattern will be highlighted in yellow. * **Lasso Selection** \- Double click on the 2D window to activate the **Lasso Selection.** \- Click around the pattern to be selected to create the Lasso Selection. \- Click the start point again to complete. \- Patterns encompassed within the Lasso Selection will be selected and highlighted in yellow. \- The patterns must be fully enclosed in the Lasso Selection to be properly selected. **Edit Pattern Tool** * **Select with Clicks** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022661887/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022661887/mceclip1.png)**Edit Pattern tool** , points and segments can be selected. Double click the point or the segment to select the entire pattern. * **Lasso Selection** ** ** \- Double click on the 2D window to activate the **Lasso Selection.** \- Click around the pattern to be selected to create the Lasso Selection. \- Click the start point again to complete. \- Patterns encompassed within the Lasso Selection will be selected and highlighted in yellow. \- The patterns must be fully enclosed in the Lasso Selection to be properly selected. **Pattern Properties** \- When the pattern is selected, its properties will appear in the **Property Editor**. **Deselect** \- Click on the 2D window to **Deselect Patterns**. \- Originally selected patterns will no longer be highlighted in yellow. **Select Multiple Patterns** \- To select multiple patterns, points, or segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select the items to be selected. **Select/Move Tool** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022723988/mceclip2.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click on the 3D pattern to select and click on the 3D window to deselect. \- To select more than one patterns, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and click on patterns to be selected. **Select All** \- To select all patterns in the 2D window, click and drag to encompass them with the marquee box. \- Or, hit the Ctrl+A keys on the keyboard to select all patterns in both 2D and 3D windows. \- When you hit the Ctrl+A keys while the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022663347/mceclip3.png) **Edit Sewing** tool is activated, all sewing lines will be selected. \- Likewise, when you hit the Ctrl+A keys while the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022725948/mceclip5.png) **Select/Move Button** tool is activated, all buttons will be selected in the 3D window. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for selecting and editing patterns in both 2D and 3D environments using various tools and methods.

title: Trace as / Convert to Internal Shape
content: **Objective** Use the **Trace** function to convert selected lines/shapes or areas into Internal Lines/Shapes. ** Location** 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005644128/Toolbar_3D_Cut_Line_Edit.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005644128/Toolbar_3D_Cut_Line_Edit.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** 2. Click on created Baselines or Internal Lines on 3D Garment. → The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now being highlighted in yellow color. 3. Right-click on the selected Baselines or Internal Lines. → A Pop-up menu appears. 4. Select **Trace as Internal** **Shape** or **Convert to Internal Shape** in the pop-up menu. → The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now being traced as /converted to Internal Shapes.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Trace function in the 3D Toolbar to convert selected lines and shapes into Internal Lines and Shapes in garment design.

content: **Objective** Rearrange tape measure according to avatar size. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005610607/___________.PNG) **Fit to Avatar** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Measure ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005610607/___________.PNG)**Fit to Avatar** 2. title: [Popup] Delete Puckering
content: **Objective** Delete unnecessary Puckering. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Puckering ▶ **Edit Puckering** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005623627/________.png) **Edit Puckering** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Puckering**▶ Edit Puckering ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005623627/________.png) **Edit Puckering** 2. Right click on top of the Puckering segment and select **Delete** , or press Delete key on keyboard. → The selected Puckering is now being deleted.

title: Optimize All Curve Points
content: ### **Objective** Optimize the number of curve points on the segments to ease the Pattern editing proces. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001059728/2.png)Edit Pattern** ### ** ****Operation** 1. Click the tool indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the 2D Pattern Window and click the **Optimize All Curve Points** , or right-click on the lines to optimize the curve points and click the **Optimize All Curve Points**. → Optimize Curve Points window appears, and the number of curve points is automatically applied as an optimized ratio. (ver 7.2) 3. Adjust the ratio of curve points. → Closer to 0%, there will be fewer curve points, but there may be deviations from the original curvature.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to optimizing curve points in the 2D Pattern editing process for improved efficiency and accuracy.

title: [Popup] Show/Hide Sewing
content: ### **Objective** When Sewing Lines are too complicated, hide them for clear view as needed. ** Location** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001219527/________.png) Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ **Hide Sewing (Selected)** /**Hide Sewing (All)** Object Browser ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) ▶ **Hide Sewing (Selected)** / **Hide Sewing (All)** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001219527/________.png) Edit Sewing ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) ▶ **Hide Sewing (Selected)** /**Hide Sewing (All)** Object Browser ▶ Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) ▶ **Hide Sewing (Selected)** / **Hide Sewing (All)** → The selected Sewing Lines or all Sewing Lines show or disappear from the 2D and the 3D window. **※ Note 1:** All Sewing Lines appear in the 2D window when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001219527/________.png) **Edit Sewing** tool is selected since the ![2D_________.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115001219507/2D_________.png) **Show 2D Sewing** tool is activated automatically. **※ Note 2:** 2D Window ▶ Show Sewing icon ▶ **Show Sewing** (ver5.0 or later)
content_description: This webpage provides instructions on how to hide sewing lines in CLO 3D for a clearer view, utilizing the 2D Toolbar and Object Browser for enhanced design clarity.

title: Flip Normal
content: **Objective** Easily flip the wrong/right side of Fabric before or after draping. Sew Patterns as desired first and flip the fabric surface at last to save time. ### ### **Location** Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Pattern ▶ **Flip Normal** ### **Operation** 1. Select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005480387/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** tool. 2. Select a Pattern to flip. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Pattern ▶ **Flip Normal** → The selected pattern's fabric surface is now being flipped over. **※ Note:** **Fold Angle** value also gets flipped when flipping normal (ver2.4.0).
content_description: "Learn how to efficiently flip the fabric surface of your patterns in Clo3D to enhance your garment draping process and save time."

title: Zipper Slider Gizmo
content: **List of Contents** Zipper Slider Gizmo Move Zipper Slider Rotate Zipper Slide **Zipper Slider Gizmo** \- Rotate or move slider to adjust its distance from zipper tape using its Gizmo. \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002238927/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png)**Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and select the slider. **Move Zipper Slider** \- While the Simulation is deactivated, click the Zipper slider to be moved to access the Gizmo. \- Click and drag the blue segment of the Gizmo to move the slider back and forth. \- Sliders cannot be moved vertically and horizontally. **Rotate Zipper Slide** \- While the Simulation is deactivated, click the Zipper slider to be rotated to access the Gizmo. \- Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the Gizmo to rotate on X axis. \- Click and drag the blue circle of the Gizmo to rotate on Y axis. \- Click and drag the red circle of the Gizmo to rotate on Z axis. \- To rotate the puller only, click the puller again while the slider is selected. \- The puller is highlighted in yellow and the Gizmo changes. \- To reset the slider’s position and angle, right click on the slider and select **Reset Slider Arrangement**. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions on how to use the Zipper Slider Gizmo to move and rotate zipper sliders effectively in your design projects.

title: Seamline Topstitch
content: **Seamline Topstitch ** **-** Establish the Topstitch along the Seamlines. \- Select the ![2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001043407/2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg)**Seamline Topstitch** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Material ▶ **Seamline Topstitch**. \- With the Seamline Topstitch tool activated, all the Seamlines appear in the 2D Window. \- Hover over the desired Seamline. \- A blue guide point should appear and click and drag along the Seamline. \- Click again to complete the Seamline Topstitch. \- The Seamline Topstitch created on the Seamlines should be highlighted in red. \- The ![2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001043407/2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg)**Seamline Topstitch** tool creates the Topstitch along both sides of the paired Seamlines. Therefore, the blue guide point will appear on both sides of the paired Seamlines. \- The ![2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001043407/2015-09-10____11-06-11.jpg)**Seamline Topstitch** tool has some similar qualities with the Free Topstitch tool. Users do not have to select the entire segment of the Seamline. Divide up the Seamlines to apply multiple styles of the Seamline Topstitch on the selected pair of the Seamlines.
content_description: Learn how to effectively use the Seamline Topstitch tool to create and customize topstitching along seamlines in your designs.

title: Create Seam Allowance
content: ### **Objective** Create seam allowances on Patterns. ** Location ** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Seam Allowance ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![seam_allowance.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024213967/seam_allowance.png) **Seam Allowance** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Seam Allowance ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![seam_allowance.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024213967/seam_allowance.png) **Seam Allowance** 2. Click on the Pattern outline where seam allowance should be added. → Seam allowance is added and colored in grey. **※Note:** Direct editing is not allowed for seam allowances. To edit them, please [edit](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000607387-2D-%ED%8C%A8%ED%84%B4-%EC%88%98%EC%A0%95) Pattern outlines,
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for adding seam allowances to patterns using the 2D Pattern tool in CLO 3D.

title: Convert to Segment Point
content: **Convert to Segment Point** \- Convert a curve point to a segment point \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021911588/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a curve point and select **Convert to Segment Point** from the pop-up menu. ** **\- The selected curve point will be converted to a segment point.
content_description: This web page provides a quick guide on how to convert a curve point to a segment point using the Edit Curve Point tool in the 2D window.
